title: Safe cleanup
when_to_use: Clean up WordPress, unused plugins, unused media, site feels cluttered or slow from cruft.
principles: Report first, mutate second — give a prioritized checklist before deleting anything.
Prefer deactivate over uninstall until the user confirms they want files gone.
Unused-media findings are heuristic (not featured/logo/in content) — never bulk-delete without HITL; bulk delete may be Premium.
Do not deactivate security, backup, or ecommerce plugins without a clear user request and warning.
Cleanup is not the same as “install a cleaner plugin” — prefer native Ahentic scans.
steps: list-plugins: flag inactive plugins and obvious overlap (multiple SEO/cache/security).
get-site-health for environment issues that look like “cruft” but are config.
find-unused-media for a capped unused-image report with links to the media library.
Present safe actions: deactivate unused plugins (HITL), review media before delete, leave backups alone.
Only uninstall when the user clearly wants removal after deactivate; one at a time with HITL.
If bulk delete / orphan-link repair abilities are missing: report findings and use missing_ability — do not fake bulk deletes.
anti_patterns: Uninstalling a pile of plugins in one shot without a report.
Deleting media that might be used in page builders/CSS not visible to the scanner — warn about false positives.
Installing “WP cleanup” plugins as the default answer.
Touching payment, membership, or security plugins casually.
